correctness.rationale: The Prüfer-code occupancy representation is an exact bijection. The k_n transition entails k_n→∞, n/k_n!→eλ and k_n²/n→0. Joint rare occupancy probabilities give λ^r factorial moments. Conditional on r specified rare boxes, the exact remaining-box occupancy formula yields leaf-mean bias (r/e)k_n. The nonstandard crucial step—a summable bound |Cov(L_n,(H_n)_{underline r})| ≤ C r(k_n+2)(n/k_n!)^r—is proved using bounded derivatives of b(1−1/b)^t and multinomial falling-factorial moment identities. Dominated finite inclusion-exclusion gives the coefficient λe^(−λ−1). The standalone checker reproduced 45 exact-rational validations including all small Prüfer codes; these are supporting checks, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact new scope is the logarithmic-threshold normalized covariance and conditional leaf-mean split. Janson 2011 provides the same maximum-degree critical regime (Theorem 18.23, Example 18.24), and fixed-degree Gaussian limits (Section 20.2), but neither gives a mixed mean correction on the smaller k_n scale. Carr et al. 1994 address labeled-tree maximum-degree distributions; their full text is unavailable and remains a genuine historical priority risk. published-finding corpus queries for the exact conditional shift, occupancy aliases, and related fixed-degree profile found different statements, not a stronger result implying this coefficient.
residual_risks: The complete 1994 Carr–Goh–Schmutz article was inaccessible; only the marginal maximum-degree abstract and bibliographic references were inspected. An implicit stronger mixed occupancy/leaf result cannot be excluded.
A broader occupancy extremal theorem or unpublished source might imply the coefficient without matching the claim wording; independent historical priority review is still needed.

value.rationale: The number of leaves and maximum degree are standard, independently motivated global descriptors of a uniform labeled tree. The sharp degree transition is a natural, non-arbitrary threshold; the new positive k_n-order difference in conditional expected leaves diverges but is invisible at ordinary sqrt(n) CLT scale. Its exact λ exp(−λ−1) coefficient gives meaningful second-scale dependence information and is not merely a normalization check, fixed-label special case, or finite table recomputation. Generality beyond Cayley trees is not claimed.
